questions.title: Vitamin cofactor for proline/lysine hydroxylation
questions.question: Which vitamin is required for hydroxylation of proline and lysine in collagen synthesis?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Vitamin D governs calcium/phosphate handling and bone mineralisation, not the hydroxylation chemistry of collagen's own polypeptide chain.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Vitamin K is a cofactor for gamma-carboxylation of glutamate residues in clotting factors and some bone matrix proteins, an entirely different post-translational reaction.
explanations.C: Correct. Prolyl hydroxylase and lysyl hydroxylase, the intracellular enzymes that hydroxylate proline and lysine residues on the procollagen alpha-chain in the rough endoplasmic reticulum, require vitamin C (L-ascorbic acid) as a cofactor to keep their iron centre in the reduced (Fe2+) state. Without vitamin C the hydroxylation reaction stalls, which is why scurvy presents with defective, poorly cross-linked collagen. Molecular oxygen and ferrous iron are also required, but vitamin C is the classic, exam-tested cofactor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Vitamin A is relevant to epithelial differentiation and vision, not to collagen's hydroxylation step.

questions.learning_objective: Name vitamin C as the cofactor for collagen's prolyl/lysyl hydroxylases.

questions.title: Lysyl oxidase function
questions.question: Which of the following best describes the lysyl oxidase enzyme?

options.A: Required for allysine synthesis in collagen
options.C: Catalyses oxidative deamination of lysine side chains into allysine

explanations.A: Incorrect alone. This is true of lysyl oxidase, but it is not the only correct statement -- the enzyme is also copper-dependent and its mechanism is specifically oxidative deamination, so 'all of the above' captures the full picture.
explanations.B: Incorrect alone. Lysyl oxidase does require copper as a cofactor, but this statement alone omits the enzyme's actual catalytic action and product, so the complete answer is 'all of the above'.
explanations.C: Incorrect alone. This correctly names the reaction lysyl oxidase catalyses, but it leaves out the cofactor requirement and the resulting allysine product description, both of which are also true.
explanations.D: Correct. Lysyl oxidase is a copper-dependent, extracellular enzyme that oxidatively deaminates the side chains of specific lysine and hydroxylysine residues on tropocollagen, converting them to reactive aldehydes (allysine). These aldehydes then spontaneously condense with neighbouring residues to form the covalent cross-links that give mature collagen fibrils their tensile strength, so every one of the three statements is correct.

questions.learning_objective: Describe lysyl oxidase's cofactor, substrate and product in collagen cross-linking.

questions.title: Scurvy -- which statement is false
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about scurvy?

options.A: It is due to vitamin C deficiency in the diet for a few days
options.B: Hydroxylation of proline and lysine will be deficient
options.C: Collagen is weak due to decreased hydrogen bonds
options.D: The patient shows bleeding gums and delayed wound healing

explanations.A: Correct as the false statement. Scurvy does not develop after only a few days of dietary vitamin C deprivation. The body's vitamin C stores (in liver and other tissues) typically take several weeks to a few months of deficient intake to deplete before clinical scurvy appears, so a few days is far too short a window.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Vitamin C is the required cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase, so its deficiency directly impairs hydroxylation of proline and lysine during collagen synthesis.
explanations.C: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Under-hydroxylated collagen chains form fewer of the hydrogen bonds that stabilise the triple helix, so the resulting collagen is structurally weak.
explanations.D: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Bleeding gums, poor wound healing and easy bruising are the classic clinical presentation of scurvy, reflecting weak, poorly cross-linked collagen in gingival and connective tissue.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the false statement among scurvy's mechanism and presentation, including the realistic time course of vitamin C depletion.

questions.title: Collagen structure -- which statement is false
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about collagen?

options.A: The chain contains approximately 1000 amino acids
options.B: Glycine is repeated every third position
options.C: It has a repeated sequence Gly-X-Y
options.D: Proline disrupts collagen helix as an alpha helix

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Each collagen alpha-chain is indeed roughly 1000 amino acid residues long.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Glycine, the smallest amino acid, occupies every third position in the chain -- this is required so it can fit at the crowded centre of the triple helix.
explanations.C: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Collagen's primary structure is a repeating Gly-X-Y motif, with proline and hydroxyproline frequently occupying the X and Y positions.
explanations.D: Correct as the false statement. Collagen is not an alpha helix at all -- proline's rigid ring structure and the requirement for interchain (not intrachain) hydrogen bonding between the three supercoiled strands make collagen's triple helix a structurally distinct, further-wound helix, so describing proline as disrupting 'collagen helix as alpha helix' misstates collagen's actual structure rather than a true disruptive effect on a genuine alpha helix. This is exactly why the Gly-X-Y repeat and interchain hydrogen bonding, not an alpha-helical intrachain scheme, define collagen's stability.

questions.learning_objective: State the Gly-X-Y repeat and chain-length facts about collagen and recognise that collagen is not a classical alpha helix.

questions.title: Order of collagen synthesis steps
questions.question: The following are steps of collagen synthesis: 1) Glycosylation of some hydroxylysine; 2) Hydroxylation of proline and lysine; 3) Cleavage of the signal sequence of preprocollagen in the rough endoplasmic reticulum; 4) Extracellular cleavage of procollagen molecules; 5) Assembly and secretion of procollagen to the extracellular space. Which is the correct sequence?

explanations.A: Incorrect. This places glycosylation before signal-peptide cleavage and hydroxylation, but the signal sequence must be cleaved first and hydroxylation must precede glycosylation of hydroxylysine (glycosylation modifies a residue hydroxylation has already created).
explanations.B: Incorrect. This places extracellular cleavage (step 4) before secretion (step 5), which is impossible -- procollagen cannot be cleaved extracellularly before it has been secreted from the cell.
explanations.C: Correct. Synthesis runs: cleave the preprocollagen signal sequence (3) -> hydroxylate proline and lysine (2) -> glycosylate hydroxylysine (1) -> assemble and secrete procollagen (5) -> cleave procollagen extracellularly (4). This is exactly the intracellular-then-extracellular order the pathway follows.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This swaps the order of secretion (5) and extracellular cleavage (4) -- cleavage of procollagen happens extracellularly after secretion, not before it.

questions.learning_objective: Sequence the intracellular and extracellular steps of collagen synthesis in order.

questions.title: Residue hydroxylated during collagen maturation
questions.question: Which of the following is hydroxylated during collagen maturation?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Glycine's role is structural (it occupies every third position so the triple helix can pack tightly); it is not a substrate for the hydroxylase enzymes.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cysteine is essentially absent from mature triple-helical collagen and is not a hydroxylation substrate.
explanations.C: Correct. Both proline and lysine residues are hydroxylated by vitamin-C-dependent hydroxylases during collagen maturation in the rough endoplasmic reticulum; lysine hydroxylation produces hydroxylysine, which also serves as the site for subsequent glycosylation. This distinguishes hydroxylation, an intracellular vitamin-C-dependent step, from the later extracellular cross-linking step performed by a different enzyme.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Arginine is not a substrate for collagen's hydroxylase enzymes; it plays a role elsewhere in metabolism (e.g. as a substrate in creatine synthesis via AGAT), not in collagen hydroxylation.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Leucine is not modified during collagen maturation.

questions.learning_objective: Name lysine (alongside proline) as a hydroxylation substrate in collagen maturation.

questions.title: Intracellular event during collagen maturation
questions.question: Which of the following events occurs inside the cell during collagen maturation?

options.A: Removal of the N-terminal propeptide of procollagen
options.B: Removal of the C-terminal propeptide of procollagen
options.E: Formation of disulfide bonds at the terminal pro-sequences

explanations.A: Incorrect. Removal of the N-terminal propeptide happens extracellularly, after procollagen has already been secreted, by a procollagen N-peptidase.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Removal of the C-terminal propeptide is likewise an extracellular event, occurring after secretion.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Conversion of lysine (and hydroxylysine) side chains to allysine is catalysed by lysyl oxidase, an extracellular enzyme, so this step happens outside the cell.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cross-link formation between tropocollagen molecules follows lysyl oxidase's extracellular action and is itself extracellular.
explanations.E: Correct. Interchain disulfide bonds form at the C-terminal propeptide region of the three procollagen chains while they are still inside the rough endoplasmic reticulum; this disulfide-bond-driven chain alignment is what allows the three chains to correctly register and begin winding into the triple helix before secretion. This intracellular alignment step precedes and enables every later maturation event, including secretion and extracellular cross-linking.

questions.learning_objective: Separate the intracellular chain-alignment/disulfide step from the extracellular propeptide-cleavage and cross-linking steps of collagen maturation.

questions.title: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome -- which statement is false
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding Ehlers-Danlos syndrome?

options.C: The most serious form is vascular
options.D: Replacement of glycine by a bulky amino acid

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is a group of inherited disorders affecting fibrillar collagens, commonly type I, III or V.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Hyperextensible, fragile skin is one of the classic clinical features of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
explanations.C: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). The vascular type (type IV, from a COL3A1 defect) is the most serious form, carrying the highest risk of arterial and organ rupture.
explanations.D: Correct as the false statement. Substitution of a bulky amino acid for one of collagen's obligatory Gly-X-Y glycines is the classic mechanism of osteogenesis imperfecta (a type I collagen gene mutation), not the typical mechanism of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, which more often arises from defects in collagen-processing enzymes (e.g. deficient procollagen peptidase or lysyl hydroxylase) or from collagen gene mutations that do not specifically target the Gly-X-Y glycine.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the false statement about Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and distinguish its mechanism from osteogenesis imperfecta's.

questions.title: Collagen architecture in teeth
questions.question: What is the structural arrangement of collagen in teeth (dentine)?

explanations.A: Correct. Like tendon, dentine's collagen is packed as parallel bundles of fibres, an arrangement that gives tensile strength along a defined axis -- the same mechanical logic that governs tendon architecture. This is the same packing logic that makes tendon collagen strong along its long axis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A gel arrangement is characteristic of the vitreous humor, where transparency and cushioning matter more than directional tensile strength.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A near-crystalline, regularly spaced fibril arrangement is characteristic of the cornea, where it is needed for optical transparency, not of dentine.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A random meshwork is more characteristic of loose connective tissue or basement membrane (type IV collagen), not of the highly ordered collagen in dentine.

questions.learning_objective: Match collagen's tissue-specific fibril packing to the tissue's mechanical role, for teeth/tendon versus vitreous humor versus cornea.

questions.title: Collagen architecture in vitreous humor
questions.question: What is the structural arrangement of collagen in the vitreous humor?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Parallel fibre bundles are characteristic of tendon and dentine, tissues that need directional tensile strength, not of the vitreous humor.
explanations.B: Correct. In the vitreous humor, collagen (together with hyaluronic acid) forms a loose, hydrated gel network rather than densely packed fibrils, giving the eye's vitreous chamber its transparency and its shock-absorbing, cushioning consistency without rigid structure. This gel arrangement is very different from the crystalline packing seen in the cornea, which instead prioritises optical clarity.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Near-crystalline, regularly spaced packing is characteristic of the cornea, not the vitreous humor.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A random meshwork better describes loose connective tissue or basement membrane, not the vitreous humor's specific gel arrangement.

questions.learning_objective: State that collagen forms a loose gel arrangement in the vitreous humor, matching that tissue's need for transparency and cushioning.

questions.title: Lysyl oxidase cofactor
questions.question: Lysyl oxidase enzyme needs which of the following as a cofactor?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Iron (ferrous) is a cofactor for the intracellular prolyl/lysyl hydroxylases, a different enzyme step, not for lysyl oxidase.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Magnesium is not the cofactor associated with collagen cross-linking chemistry.
explanations.C: Correct. Lysyl oxidase is a copper-dependent extracellular enzyme; a dietary or genetic copper deficiency directly reduces its activity and weakens collagen cross-linking. This is why copper deficiency (or a copper-transport defect, as in Menkes disease) weakens collagen cross-linking specifically, sparing the earlier hydroxylation step.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Zinc is not lysyl oxidase's cofactor, though it is a cofactor for many other enzymes (e.g. some matrix metalloproteinases involved in collagen turnover, a different process).

questions.learning_objective: Name copper as lysyl oxidase's cofactor.

questions.title: Step impaired by vitamin C deficiency
questions.question: Which of the following steps in collagen synthesis would be impaired in a patient with vitamin C deficiency?

options.A: Removal of the N-terminal signal peptide
options.D: Extracellular assembly of tropocollagen molecules into collagen fibrils

explanations.A: Incorrect. Signal-peptide cleavage is a co-translational/early processing event that does not require vitamin C.
explanations.B: Correct. Vitamin C is required by prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase; without adequate hydroxylation, the chains are under-hydroxylated, which impairs both the stability of the triple helix itself (fewer stabilising interactions) and the downstream cross-link formation, since inadequately hydroxylated/glycosylated chains do not mature normally into cross-linkable fibrils. Vitamin C deficiency therefore has a cascading effect on collagen quality rather than blocking a single isolated step.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Exocytosis (secretion) of procollagen-containing vesicles is a general cellular trafficking process, not specifically dependent on vitamin C.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Extracellular fibril assembly of tropocollagen is a self-assembly/packing process; while downstream of vitamin-C-dependent hydroxylation in the pathway, it is lysyl oxidase's cross-linking (copper-dependent) that most directly governs fibril integrity at that extracellular stage, not vitamin C directly.

questions.learning_objective: Trace how a vitamin C deficiency at the hydroxylation step propagates to impair triple-helix stability and cross-linking.

questions.title: Collagen stability -- which statement is false
questions.question: All of the following play a role in collagen stability, EXCEPT:

options.A: Each chain is coiled left-handed and the three chains are supercoiled right-handed
options.B: Intrachain hydrogen bonding in each chain of the tropocollagen
options.C: Cross-link formation in the triple helix

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Each collagen alpha-chain is itself a left-handed helix, and the three chains then supercoil together into a right-handed triple helix -- this dual-handedness is part of what gives collagen its mechanical stability.
explanations.B: Correct as the exception. Collagen's triple helix is stabilised mainly by interchain hydrogen bonds (between the NH of glycine on one chain and the C=O of a residue on an adjacent chain), not by intrachain hydrogen bonding -- intrachain hydrogen bonding is instead the stabilising mechanism of a classical alpha helix, which collagen is not. This distinction between interchain and intrachain bonding is the single most commonly tested structural fact separating collagen from a true alpha helix.
explanations.C: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Lysyl-oxidase-mediated cross-link formation between tropocollagen molecules is a major contributor to mature collagen's tensile strength and stability.
explanations.D: Incorrect (i.e. this statement is true). Interchain hydrogen bonds between the three strands of the triple helix are a genuine stabilising force in collagen's structure.

questions.learning_objective: Identify interchain (not intrachain) hydrogen bonding as the stabilising interaction in collagen's triple helix.

questions.title: Classic Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome collagen defect
questions.question: The classic form of Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome (EDS) is due to a defect in which collagen type?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Type IV collagen is a basement-membrane (network-forming, not fibrillar) collagen; its defects underlie diseases such as Alport syndrome, not classic EDS.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Type III is a fibrillar collagen and is implicated in the vascular type of EDS (type IV EDS), but the classic form of EDS is most closely associated with type V (and type I) collagen abnormalities, not type III specifically as the primary classic-form defect.
explanations.C: Correct. Classic EDS most often results from mutations affecting type V collagen (COL5A1/COL5A2), which forms a minor fibrillar component that regulates the assembly of type I collagen fibrils; its defect produces the joint hypermobility, skin hyperextensibility and 'cigarette-paper' scarring typical of the classic form. Recognising type V (alongside type I) as the classic-form defect separates it from the type III/IV associations of the vascular form.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Type IX is a fibril-associated collagen (FACIT) that decorates the surface of type II collagen fibrils in cartilage; it is not the collagen type implicated in classic EDS.

questions.learning_objective: Name type V collagen as the classic-form Ehlers-Danlos defect, distinguishing it from the vascular type's type III/IV associations.

questions.title: Osteogenesis imperfecta mutation type
questions.question: Osteogenesis imperfecta is due to which type of mutation?

explanations.A: Correct. Osteogenesis imperfecta is typically caused by a dominant-negative missense point mutation in COL1A1 or COL1A2 that substitutes a bulkier amino acid for one of the obligatory glycine residues in the Gly-X-Y repeat, distorting the triple helix from that point onward and, because type I collagen is a heterotrimer, poisoning the whole molecule even though only one allele is affected. A single abnormal chain is therefore enough to disrupt an entire triple helix, explaining the disease's dominant inheritance.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A silent mutation changes the DNA sequence without altering the encoded amino acid, so it would not produce a structurally defective protein at all.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A nonsense mutation introduces a premature stop codon; this generally causes a much shorter, often non-functional or degraded chain rather than the single-residue distortion that is osteogenesis imperfecta's characteristic mechanism.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A frame-shift mutation scrambles the entire downstream reading frame, which would produce a grossly abnormal protein rather than the single, localised glycine substitution that is the hallmark mechanism here.

questions.learning_objective: Name missense point mutation as osteogenesis imperfecta's typical mutation type and explain the glycine-substitution mechanism.

questions.title: Lysyl hydroxylase cofactors
questions.question: Lysyl hydroxylase enzyme needs all the following compounds EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this is needed). Vitamin C is required by lysyl hydroxylase (and prolyl hydroxylase) to keep the enzyme's iron centre in the active reduced state.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this is needed). Molecular oxygen is a direct substrate of the hydroxylation reaction, which incorporates one oxygen atom into the hydroxyl group formed.
explanations.C: Correct as the exception. Copper is not a cofactor of lysyl hydroxylase -- copper is instead the cofactor of the extracellular enzyme lysyl oxidase, a completely separate, later step in collagen maturation (cross-linking rather than hydroxylation). Confusing these two 'lysyl' enzymes and their two different cofactors is the classic trap this question tests.
explanations.D: Incorrect (i.e. this is needed). Ferrous iron (Fe2+) is required at the enzyme's active site for the hydroxylation reaction to proceed.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish lysyl hydroxylase's cofactors (vitamin C, O2, Fe2+) from lysyl oxidase's cofactor (copper), and recognise copper is not a hydroxylase cofactor.

questions.title: Timing of collagen glycation
questions.question: Glycation of collagen occurs:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Glycosylation acts on hydroxylysine, a residue that does not exist until hydroxylation has already occurred, so glycation cannot precede hydroxylation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Glycosylation of hydroxylysine happens before the three chains assemble into the triple helix, not after.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Glycation of collagen is an intracellular event, occurring in the rough endoplasmic reticulum, not extracellularly and not after the collagen molecule is already mature.
explanations.D: Correct. Once proline and lysine have been hydroxylated intracellularly, some of the resulting hydroxylysine residues are glycosylated (with glucose and/or galactose) while the chains are still inside the cell and before the triple helix has fully assembled -- glycation is therefore intracellular and sequentially downstream of hydroxylation. Placing glycation correctly in this intracellular, post-hydroxylation window is what distinguishes it from the later extracellular cross-linking step.

questions.learning_objective: Place glycation of collagen as an intracellular event occurring after hydroxylation but before triple-helix assembly.

questions.title: Site of collagen glycation
questions.question: Glycation of collagen occurs on which residue?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Hydroxyproline is a product of proline hydroxylation, but it is not the residue that carries the glucose/galactose sugar in collagen glycosylation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Allysine is the product of lysyl oxidase's oxidative deamination step, an entirely separate, later, extracellular reaction, not the site of glycosylation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Glycine's role is purely structural (packing at the triple-helix core); it is not glycosylated.
explanations.D: Correct. Glucose and/or galactose sugars are attached to the hydroxyl group of hydroxylysine residues -- this is exactly why collagen is classified as a glycoprotein. No other residue in the chain carries this sugar attachment.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Unmodified proline is not the glycosylation site; only the hydroxylated lysine derivative (hydroxylysine) carries the sugar.

questions.learning_objective: Name hydroxylysine as the residue that carries collagen's glycosylation, explaining why collagen is a glycoprotein.

questions.title: Amino acid absent from mature collagen
questions.question: Which of the following amino acids is absent from mature collagen?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Glycine is abundant in mature collagen, occupying every third position of the Gly-X-Y repeat.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Proline is a common residue in the X/Y positions of mature collagen.
explanations.C: Correct. Cysteine is essentially absent from the triple-helical body of mature collagen; it exists only in the terminal propeptides of procollagen, which are cleaved off extracellularly and are not part of the mature, cross-linked fibril. This is why cysteine-based disulfide chemistry is confined to the propeptide region rather than the mature collagen fibril itself.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hydroxylysine is present in mature collagen and is, in fact, the glycosylation site that makes collagen a glycoprotein.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Hydroxyproline is abundant in mature collagen and is one of its most distinctive residues, frequently used as a biochemical marker of collagen content.

questions.learning_objective: State that cysteine is essentially absent from mature triple-helical collagen (present only in the cleaved propeptides).

questions.title: Location of lysyl oxidase's action
questions.question: Lysyl oxidase enzyme causes oxidative deamination of lysine in which location?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The ribosome is the site of translation, not of any post-translational collagen modification.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The rough endoplasmic reticulum is where the intracellular steps (signal cleavage, hydroxylation, glycosylation, disulfide-bond chain alignment) happen, not lysyl oxidase's cross-linking step.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The Golgi apparatus is involved in trafficking secretory vesicles, not in lysyl oxidase's catalytic action.
explanations.D: Correct. Lysyl oxidase is an extracellular, copper-dependent enzyme; it acts on tropocollagen molecules after they have been secreted and assembled into fibrils, oxidatively deaminating lysine/hydroxylysine side chains to allysine in the extracellular fluid/matrix. This extracellular location is what separates lysyl oxidase from the intracellular hydroxylases that act earlier in the same pathway.

questions.learning_objective: State that lysyl oxidase acts extracellularly, distinguishing it from the intracellular hydroxylation/glycosylation steps.

questions.title: Most common amino acid in collagen
questions.question: Which of the following is the most common amino acid in collagen's structure?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Proline is common (frequently occupying the X position of Gly-X-Y) but is less abundant overall than glycine.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Hydroxyproline is characteristic of collagen but is not its most abundant residue.
explanations.C: Correct. Because glycine occupies every third position along the entire ~1000-residue chain (the Gly-X-Y repeat), it makes up roughly one-third of all residues, making it collagen's single most common amino acid. No other single residue approaches glycine's share of the chain.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hydroxylysine is present but in much smaller amounts than glycine.

questions.learning_objective: Name glycine as collagen's most common amino acid, as a direct consequence of the Gly-X-Y repeat.

questions.title: Which statement about collagen structure is true
questions.question: Which of the following statements is true?

options.B: In an alpha helix, each turn contains three amino acids
options.C: Intrachain hydrogen bonds stabilise the collagen helix
options.D: Glycine is present in every third position in the collagen helix

explanations.A: Incorrect. Proline is a normal, expected component of collagen's X/Y positions and helps stabilise (rather than disrupt) the triple helix by restricting backbone rotation; it would disrupt a classical alpha helix, but that is a different structure from collagen.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A classical alpha helix turn contains roughly 3.6 residues, not exactly three -- this is a true fact about alpha helices in general, but stated imprecisely here, and in any case collagen itself is not an alpha helix.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Collagen's triple helix is stabilised mainly by interchain hydrogen bonds between the three strands, not by intrachain hydrogen bonds within a single chain (which is instead the stabilising mechanism of a true alpha helix).
explanations.D: Correct. Glycine occupies every third position along each collagen alpha-chain, the defining feature of the Gly-X-Y repeat, because it is the only amino acid small enough to fit at the crowded centre of the triple helix. This packing requirement is the direct structural reason collagen cannot be a classical alpha helix.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the single true statement among several collagen/alpha-helix structural claims, correctly separating collagen's triple helix from a classical alpha helix.

questions.title: Copper deficiency and collagen formation
questions.question: Deficiency of copper affects the formation of normal collagen by reducing the activity of:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Glucosyl transferase adds glucose during hydroxylysine glycosylation; it is not copper-dependent.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Galactosyl transferase adds galactose during hydroxylysine glycosylation; it is likewise not copper-dependent.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Lysyl hydroxylase requires vitamin C, molecular oxygen and ferrous iron, not copper.
explanations.D: Correct. Lysyl oxidase is the copper-dependent enzyme in collagen maturation; a copper deficiency directly reduces its activity, impairing the extracellular cross-linking step and weakening mature collagen. The hydroxylation step upstream, by contrast, depends on vitamin C and iron rather than copper.
explanations.E: Incorrect. Proline hydroxylase, like lysyl hydroxylase, requires vitamin C, oxygen and ferrous iron, not copper.

questions.learning_objective: Name lysyl oxidase as the copper-dependent enzyme whose reduced activity explains copper-deficiency collagen defects.

questions.title: Cofactor for hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine formation
questions.question: Which of the following is involved in the formation of hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine during collagen synthesis?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Biotin is a cofactor for carboxylase enzymes (e.g. in fatty acid synthesis and gluconeogenesis), unrelated to collagen hydroxylation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Copper is the cofactor for the later, extracellular lysyl oxidase cross-linking step, not for hydroxylation of proline and lysine.
explanations.C: Correct. Prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases require vitamin C (ascorbic acid) to keep their iron centre active, producing hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine respectively -- this is the same cofactor whose deficiency causes scurvy's collagen defects. The later, separate cross-linking step instead depends on copper, not vitamin C.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Vitamin B12 is a cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and methionine synthase reactions, unrelated to collagen hydroxylation.

questions.learning_objective: Reconfirm vitamin C as the cofactor producing hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine in collagen synthesis.

questions.title: Procollagen biosynthesis -- which event is extracellular
questions.question: All of the following events in procollagen biosynthesis occur within cells, EXCEPT:

explanations.A: Incorrect (i.e. this is intracellular). Disulfide-bond-driven chain alignment of the three procollagen chains happens inside the rough endoplasmic reticulum, before secretion.
explanations.B: Incorrect (i.e. this is intracellular). O-linked glycosylation of hydroxylysine occurs intracellularly, after hydroxylation and before secretion.
explanations.C: Correct as the exception. Oxidation of lysyl residues (to allysine) is catalysed by lysyl oxidase, a copper-dependent enzyme that acts extracellularly on secreted, assembled tropocollagen -- this is the one listed event that is NOT intracellular. Every other listed event -- chain alignment, glycosylation, and disulfide bond formation -- happens earlier, inside the cell.
explanations.D: Incorrect (i.e. this is intracellular). Hydroxylation of lysyl (and prolyl) residues is catalysed by the vitamin-C-dependent hydroxylases inside the cell.
explanations.E: Incorrect (i.e. this is intracellular). Disulfide bond formation at the C-terminal propeptides occurs intracellularly, aligning the three chains before triple-helix formation.

questions.learning_objective: Identify oxidation of lysyl residues (lysyl oxidase) as the one procollagen-biosynthesis event that is extracellular, not intracellular.

questions.title: Order of collagen molecule progression
questions.question: The following are steps of collagen synthesis: 1) Collagen fibril; 2) Prochain; 3) Preprochain; 4) Procollagen; 5) Tropocollagen. Which is the correct sequence?

explanations.A: Correct. The molecule progresses preprochain (3, with its signal peptide still attached) -> prochain (2, after signal-peptide cleavage) -> procollagen (4, the assembled triple helix with propeptides still attached) -> tropocollagen (5, after extracellular propeptide cleavage) -> collagen fibril (1, after lysyl-oxidase cross-linking assembles the mature fibril). Each named intermediate therefore marks a distinct processing milestone, from the earliest signal-peptide-bearing form to the final cross-linked fibril.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This swaps the order of procollagen (4) and tropocollagen (5) -- procollagen still carries its terminal propeptides and must be converted to tropocollagen by their cleavage, not the reverse.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This places prochain (2) before preprochain (3), but the preprochain (still carrying its signal peptide) is the earliest form; the signal peptide must be cleaved first to give the prochain.
explanations.D: Incorrect. This both reverses preprochain/prochain order and skips tropocollagen as an intermediate before the fibril, omitting the extracellular propeptide-cleavage step entirely.

questions.learning_objective: Sequence collagen's named intermediate forms from preprochain through to the mature fibril.
